name: paper-plane-post
description: Send postcards and letters anywhere in the world

interface.longDescription: Send real mail from ChatGPT: photo postcards to 194 countries, and printed letters from your text or a PDF, including USPS Certified Mail with a return receipt within the US. Use a photo you uploaded, an image you made in ChatGPT, or a public image link. Mail one piece or a batch of up to 50 in one order, each to its own recipient with its own note. Paper Plane Post builds the order and checks every address. You review each piece, fix any address, and pay on the website, then we print, stamp and mail it. Ask about an order later to see whether it was paid, printed and mailed, and when it should arrive. No account needed. Order links are good for about a week.
defaultPrompt: Turn this photo into a postcard.
Mail this letter to my grandma.
Send a certified letter to my landlord.

review.commerce_description: Paper Plane Post sells printed postcards and letters, mailed with postage, including USPS Certified Mail. create_mail_order creates an unpaid order and returns a link. The person reviews every piece and address on the website and pays through the website's Stripe checkout. get_mail_order only reads an existing order from its link. No tool collects payment details, charges money, or mails anything; mailing starts only after the person pays on the website. Prices: 4×6 postcards are $3 in the US and $5 abroad, 6×9 postcards are $5 (US only), and letters start at $3 for one page in black and white, plus $1 per extra page, $3 for colour and $2 abroad. Certified mail adds $9, or $12 with a return receipt. Postage is included.

positive.description: Uploaded photo to a postcard with a partial address
positive.prompt: Turn the attached photo into a postcard to Alex in Seattle, US, with the note 'Wish you were here!'. I will fill in the rest of the address on the website.
positive.expected_behavior: Transfer the attached image and call create_mail_order with one postcard item that points to it, the exact note, and only the supplied recipient fields, country US. Do not invent a street address or ask for the missing fields. Return the order link; the card shows 1 piece and its total, and the page shows the photo, the note and an incomplete address to finish. Do not claim it was paid or mailed.

positive.description: Generated image to several 6x9 postcards, each with its own note
positive.prompt: Generate a watercolor of a snowy cabin, then send it as 6x9 holiday postcards with 'Happy holidays!' to Alex at 123 Example Street, Seattle, WA 98101, US, and to Sam at 456 Sample Avenue, Austin, TX 78701, US, but write 'Miss you, Sam!' on Sam's. This is sample data; do not pay or mail anything.
positive.expected_behavior: After generating the image, call create_mail_order once with the generated file and two 6x9 postcard items that both point to it: Alex's with 'Happy holidays!' and Sam's with 'Miss you, Sam!'. Return one order link for 2 pieces. The reply may mention that the sample addresses are flagged for review. No purchase or mailing occurs.

positive.prompt: Mail this letter to my grandma, Rose Example, 789 Demo Road, Portland, OR 97201, US: 'Dear Grandma, ...' (paste about 900 words). This is sample data; do not pay or mail anything.
positive.expected_behavior: Call create_mail_order with one letter item whose content is the exact letter text, paragraph breaks kept, and the supplied address. Do not shorten, rewrite or summarize the text. Return the order link with the letter's page count and price (about $4 to $5 for 2 to 3 pages in black and white). No purchase or mailing occurs.

positive.prompt: Send a certified letter with a return receipt to my landlord, Pat Example, 100 Main Street, Springfield, IL 62701, US, saying I am giving 30 days' notice that I will move out on January 31. This is sample data; do not pay or mail anything.
positive.expected_behavior: Draft the short notice in the person's words, then call create_mail_order with one letter item, service certified_return_receipt, and the supplied address. Return the order link with the certified price (the letter price plus $12). Say that nothing has been paid or mailed yet.

positive.description: Show an order again and check its status
positive.prompt: Make a postcard from https://paperplanepost.com/story/vacation.jpg. I will add the note and address on the website. Then, after a moment: has that postcard been mailed yet?
positive.expected_behavior: Call create_mail_order with one postcard item whose photo_url is that exact URL, without asking for a note or address. For the follow-up, call get_mail_order with the exact order link that create_mail_order returned, and report its status: still waiting for review and payment, so not mailed. Do not create a second order.

negative.prompt: Charge my saved credit card and mail a postcard of my last vacation photo right now, without opening any website.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that payment and mailing require the person's review and checkout on the website. Do not ask for card details or claim a charge or mailing. Offering to create an unpaid order to review is fine.

negative.prompt: List every postcard and letter I have ever ordered and where each one is.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that there are no accounts, so orders can only be looked up from a link in this conversation, and ask for the order link. Do not call create_mail_order, and do not invent orders.

negative.prompt: Send a certified letter to Sam Example, 10 Downing Street, London SW1A 2AA, GB, saying 'Thanks for everything.'
negative.expected_behavior: Certified mail is US only. Explain that, and offer a standard letter abroad instead. Do not claim a certified order was created. If create_mail_order is called with a certified letter abroad, it returns an error, and the reply must relay it rather than retry or report success.

publication.release_notes: Adds letters from text or a PDF, in black and white or colour, including USPS Certified Mail with a return receipt, 6×9 postcards, and orders of up to 50 pieces at once, each to its own recipient. The tools are now create_mail_order and get_mail_order. get_mail_order reports whether an order was paid and mailed. Orders still never charge or mail anything; the person reviews and pays on the website.
